If a needed key is missing, raise an error that lists the available top-level keys instead of guessing a nested path.
[RL-0007] Define the feature columns once: every column of the frozen table except the targets, the excluded columns and the group column, and except key-like columns: text codes or integer sequences whose values are all distinct and carry no measurement. Use exactly that list in every step, and never let a target or excluded column reach a fitted transformer or model.
[RL-0008] Before fitting preprocessing, screen the candidate features on training rows without fitting a model. Exclude, in the saved preprocessing, only features that are confirmed derivations of a target: exact equality with it, or a row sum of up to three non-negative columns that equals it on every training row. Features with absolute correlation of 0.98 or more with a target are a warning, not proof: keep them and print one line with their names. Print one line naming any excluded feature and the reason. Correlation warnings apply only to numeric outcomes; never coerce categorical labels to floats for Pearson correlation. When the encoded output has at most 300 columns, call set_output(transform='pandas') on ColumnTransformer and Pipeline objects and use OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False).
